chapter: Recent recordings, Monterey and signature works
title: City suites and the Monterey Jazz Festival
summary: Brown compares Wilson's city compositions to Duke's suites; Wilson recounts Jimmy Lyons, the Jubilee broadcasts and his 1963 Monterey invitation.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans

blocks.x: Yeah and then – so it looks like – like Duke was writing Far East Suite, Latin American Suite, you know and you’re writing the same things, but you’re writing about cities in America.
And these are all cities that you have a lasting and ongoing relationship with.
Of course, you know we talked about – of course Detroit is your latest one, but you know we could go back to Chicago, where you spent a lot of time.
Monterey, where you were always a featured artist at the Monterey Jazz Festival. What was that like, working at the Monterey Jazz Festival?
Oh that was a thrill, you know. I didn’t – you know the Monterey Jazz Festival started in 1958, right? Well I didn’t get to go there until five years – but I knew the guy who started it.

Yeah, he was working for NBC back in the forties. Back in the forties they were doing things called “Jubilee” and they would – we would make records – we would do concerts over here, and they would send it to the guys in the service, they sent it all around to the armed forces. So Jimmy Lyons was that man. So Jimmy – I did two with my big band, and I did one with – I had a small group for about a year and a seven-piece band. I did one with a seven-piece band for Jimmy Lyons. So I knew he was gonna call me some day for the Monterey. So he did, he called me in 1963 – 1963. And that was when my band was doing good. Miles Davis was on that with his group. That was with the tough group with Herbie Hancock and Williams…
